YouTuber Tears a Rare $3.2 Million Koenigsegg Regera to Pieces After Owner Handed Him the Keys
24 photos
Photo: WhistlinDiesel | YouTube
This is the video that split the internet in two. Cody Detwiler, known online as WhistlinDiesel, destroyed one of the only 80 Koenigsegg Regeras ever built in a manner that triggered outrage among car enthusiasts and entertained those who enjoyed watching a multimillion-dollar hypercar pushed to its absolute breaking point .
Cut with a saw, nearly set on fire, and off-roaded like no tomorrow. This was the absolute abuse that a Koenigsegg Regera has gone through. The car came out of The Hamilton Collection, where it most likely spent its entire life in a climate-controlled environment.
The abuse might have served the owner’s purpose, as Steve Hamilton had already planned to have the Regera completely stripped and rebuilt into an extreme widebody, manual-swapped custom project dubbed "Project Lazarus." In his defense, Cody showed a clip of Koenigsegg CEO Christian von Koenigsegg saying, " It is cheaper to rebuild, repair, and keep on smashing the same car ."
But to car enthusiasts right here, the project got off on the wrong foot, with Steve handing over the car keys to WhistlinDiesel, along with the green light to destroy almost anything on the car except for one thing: the windshield. Replacing the Regera's specialized glass costs roughly $40,000 and is notoriously complicated. It's not like the rest is cheap…
Photo: WhistlinDiesel | YouTube Cody Detwiler, a.k.a. WhistlinDiesel, and his crew put the hybrid hypercar through a series of stunts and stress tests that the machine was probably never meant to survive, especially not one that was an eye-watering $3.2 million deal when new.
What they got on their hands was a car powered by a 5.0-liter twin-turbocharged DOHC V8 and three YASA axial-flux motors. One sits on the crankshaft and two on the rear axle shaft. The setup pushes out 1,500 horsepower (1,521 metric horsepower) and 1,475 pound-feet (2,000 Newton meters) of torque.
That is what makes the car rocket from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in 2.8 seconds, hit 124 mph (200 kph) in 6.6 seconds, and 186 mph (300 kph) in 10.9 seconds. In 2023, the Regera set a production-car world record by going from 0 to 249 mph (400 km/h) and back to a standstill in just 28.81 seconds.
The Regera features the Ghost Package, a $285,000 factory option, which brings a serious aero upgrade. The package includes an extended front splitter, front fender canards, extended side sills, and fixed rear winglets. Now, they don’t really count anymore.
Photo: WhistlinDiesel | YouTube Before heavy abuse even started, Cody and his crew noticed several glitches. The "Ghost" button on the $10,000 key fob didn’t work, opening the dihedral door caused the window to stab into the hood, and the car repeatedly shut itself off after sitting parked or switching out of EV mode.
Cody took the Regera to the track, but it did not spend much time on the tarmac. He swerved violently until he got onto the grass and proceeded to off-road the hypercar that was never supposed to drive on that sort of surface.
He powerslid and continued to roll at high speed, with a trail of dust behind him and doors wide open, basically inviting dirt into the cabin. With the Regera’s front air intakes and radiator grille full of leaves, tall grass, and debris during the off-road runs, error codes blinked on the dashboard, and the car went "beep! Beep beep!" Cody threw buckets of water over the overheating engine to cool it down.
He launched the car into a speed bump at high speed, driving both forward and backward, and dragging the speed bump itself with the front spoiler. This move blew out the front suspension and triggered more errors, causing the car to shut down. The stunt tore up the doors, mirror, and carbon fiber bits and knocked off a brake light.
Photo: WhistlinDiesel | YouTube To cause further damage, Cody stepped on the front clamshell and lay down on the engine cover as it opened. Then, they put the poor Regera on jack stands to simulate a top-speed run, but redlining the twin-turbo V8 without airflow caused the exhaust system to catch fire.
The crew repeatedly slammed the automated doors of the hypercar, jumped and sat on the carbon-fiber front clamshell, and used a saw to cut the rear spoiler in half, in what seemed the most outrageous of the abuse scenes.
The team even broke Steve Hamilton's one rule: keeping the windshield intact. Despite his warning, crew member Frankie LaPenna shattered the $40,000 windshield in a staged accident, which was cut from the video.
The $3.2 million Koenigsegg Regera is by far the most expensive car WhistlinDiesel has ever destroyed. His list includes a $400,000 Ferrari F8 Tributo, a Rolls-Royce Phantom, a Mercedes-AMG G 63 , and, added to the list in 2024, a Tesla Cybertruck. So, yes, for many car enthusiasts out there, these videos are painful to watch.
